newsitem.title: JAPAN: INSIGHT - JGBs seen fluttering near recent ranges.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - JGBs seen fluttering near recent ranges.

text.p: The key September 10-year Japanese government bond futures contract is expected to be stuck near recent ranges on Thursday, with focus on market's demand for recently launched corporate bonds, traders said.

"Demand for Tokyo Electric Power Co's (TEPCO) 10-year bonds emerged on dips, and it will be interesting to see if there will be similar demand for TEPCO and Chugoku Electric Power Co's 20-year bonds," said a trader for a trust bank's securities unit.
Market will be watching May machinery orders data due at 2 p.m. (0500 GMT) to some extent, traders said.

"The market is expecting machinery orders to increase in May by about six or seven percent from the previous month. A double-digit increase would be considered much higher than expectations and probably invite some selling," the trader for a trust bank's securities unit said.
Japan's private-sector machinery orders, excluding those for machinery at electric power firms and for ships, rose a seasonally adjusted 7.2 percent in April month-on-month.
The market's upside is likely to be limited, as some investors seem eager to unload JGBs and other bonds at around 125.50, said a trader for another trust bank's securities unit.

"There are some investors who want to unload JGBs and other domestic bonds when the September rises to around 125.50, which is also when the 2.4 percent (195th) 10-year JGB will be at par," the second trader said.
In order for the September to break convincingly above 125.50, fresh buying incentives will be needed, he said.
It would be surprising to see JGBs rise beyond expected ranges on Thursday, but one possible factor that may give JGBs strength, is weak Tokyo share prices, the first trader said.
If the key index falls below the 19,500 point level again, it may lead to buying of JGBs among dealers, he said.
